steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
Here’s a rapid rundown of the key differences between DNA and RNA:

1. Sugar backbone  
   • DNA: deoxyribose (lacks an OH on the 2′ carbon)  
   • RNA: ribose (has an OH on the 2′ carbon)

2. Nitrogenous bases  
   • DNA: A, C, G, T (thymine)  
   • RNA: A, C, G, U (uracil replaces thymine)

3. Strand structure  
   • DNA: almost always a stable double helix  
   • RNA: usually single‐stranded, can fold into complex shapes

4. Function  
   • DNA: long‐term storage of genetic information in the nucleus (and some organelles)  
   • RNA: various roles in gene expression—mRNA (messenger), tRNA (transfer), rRNA (ribosomal), regulatory RNAs

5. Stability & location  
   • DNA: chemically more stable, stays in nucleus (eukaryotes)  
   • RNA: less stable (prone to hydrolysis), found throughout the cell

In short, DNA is the stable, double‐stranded repository of genes, while RNA is the versatile, single‐stranded working copy and adapter in protein synthesis and regulation.
